Don't place your Diwali Muhurat trade before you know these timings.
This Sunday, November eighth, the market opens for just seventy minutes. Two twenty to three thirty in the afternoon. Pre-open starts at two oh five.
It's Muhurat trading. The first trade of Samvat twenty eighty three, the new year for Indian business. B S E started it in nineteen fifty seven, and N S E joined in nineteen ninety two.
And these are real trades. Whatever you buy settles like any normal day. This year, there's even a new closing auction at the end.
In the last twenty years, Nifty rose in fifteen Muhurat sessions. The biggest jump was in two thousand eight, about six percent. But nineteen of those twenty moves were smaller than one percent.

The full year matters more. Nifty ended eight of the last ten Samvat years higher, averaging about twelve percent. The best year gave thirty eight percent. The two red years lost less than three percent.
It's a tradition, not a trading signal. That's why many families buy just a small, token quantity, of a company they'd happily hold for years.
